title_en: Decision of the Supreme People's Court on Revising the Provisions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1: After the Company Law takes effect, for civil cases that have not yet been concluded by the People's Court or are newly accepted, where the civil acts or events occurred before the Company Law took effect, the laws, regulations, and judicial interpretations in effect at that time shall apply.

Article 2: Where a dispute arising from civil acts or events before the Company Law took effect is brought to the People's Court by prosecution, if the laws, regulations, and judicial interpretations in effect at that time have no explicit provisions, the relevant provisions of the Company Law may be applied by reference.

Article 3: Where the plaintiff brings a lawsuit to the People's Court on the grounds specified in Article 22(2) or Article 74(2) of the Company Law beyond the time limit prescribed by the Company Law, the People's Court shall not accept the case.

Article 4: The period of continuous shareholding of not less than 180 days as provided in Article 151 of the Company Law shall be the period of shareholding that has expired at the time when the shareholder brings a lawsuit to the People's Court; the total shareholding of not less than one percent of the company's shares as provided refers to the aggregate of the shareholding of two or more shareholders.

Article 5: Where the People's Court conducts a retrial according to law on a case that has already been finally adjudicated before the Company Law took effect, the provisions of the Company Law shall not apply.

Article 6: These Provisions shall take effect as of the date of promulgation.
Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (II)
(Adopted at the 1447th Session of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on May 5, 2008
Amended according to the Decision on Amending the Provisions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China adopted at the 1607th Session of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on February 17, 2014)
For the purpose of correctly applying the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, in light of trial practice, the following provisions are formulated concerning the application of law in cases of company dissolution and liquidation tried by the People's Court.

Article 2: Where a shareholder brings a lawsuit for dissolution of the company and simultaneously applies to the People's Court for liquidation of the company, the People's Court shall not accept the liquidation application. The People's Court may inform the plaintiff that, after the People's Court adjudicates the dissolution of the company, it may organize liquidation on its own or separately apply to the People's Court for liquidation of the company in accordance with Article 183 of the Company Law and Article 7 of these Provisions.

Article 3: Where a shareholder, when bringing a lawsuit for dissolution of the company, applies to the People's Court for property preservation or evidence preservation, the People's Court may grant the preservation provided that the shareholder provides a guarantee and the preservation does not affect the normal operation of the company.

Article 4: A shareholder bringing a lawsuit for dissolution of the company shall name the company as the defendant.
Where the plaintiff brings a lawsuit jointly against other shareholders as defendants, the People's Court shall inform the plaintiff to change the other shareholders to third parties; if the plaintiff insists on not making the change, the People's Court shall dismiss the claim against the other shareholders.
Where the plaintiff brings a lawsuit for dissolution of the company, it shall inform the other shareholders, or the People's Court shall notify them to participate in the lawsuit. Where other shareholders or interested parties apply to participate in the lawsuit as co-plaintiffs or third parties, the People's Court shall permit them.

Article 5: When trying a case of lawsuit for dissolution of a company, the People's Court shall emphasize mediation. Where the parties reach a consensus through negotiation that the company or shareholders purchase the shares, or that the company continues to exist through capital reduction, etc., and such consensus does not violate mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations, the People's Court shall support it. Where the parties cannot reach a consensus to allow the company to continue to exist, the People's Court shall timely render a judgment.
Where the People's Court mediates for the company to purchase the plaintiff's shares, the company shall transfer or cancel the shares within six months from the date the mediation document takes effect. Before the shares are transferred or canceled, the plaintiff shall not use the company's purchase of its shares as a defense against the company's creditors.

Article 6: The judgment made by the People's Court on the lawsuit for dissolution of the company shall be legally binding on all shareholders of the company.
After the People's Court dismisses the claim for dissolution of the company, if the shareholder who filed the lawsuit or another shareholder again files a lawsuit for dissolution of the company on the same facts and grounds, the People's Court shall not accept the case.

Article 10: Before the company completes liquidation according to law and undergoes cancellation registration, any civil lawsuit concerning the company shall be conducted in the name of the company.
Where the company has established a liquidation group, the person in charge of the liquidation group shall represent the company in participating in the lawsuit; if no liquidation group has been established, the original legal representative shall represent the company in participating in the lawsuit.

Article 11: When the company is liquidated, the liquidation group shall, in accordance with Article 185 of the Company Law, notify all known creditors in writing of the matters concerning company dissolution and liquidation, and make an announcement in a newspaper of national circulation or a provincial newspaper of influence in the place where the company is registered, depending on the company's size and business territory.
Where the liquidation group fails to fulfill the obligation of notification and announcement as provided in the preceding paragraph, resulting in a creditor failing to declare its claims in time and thus not being satisfied, and the creditor claims that the liquidation group members shall bear compensation liability for the losses caused thereby, the People's Court shall support the claim according to law.

Article 12: Where, during the liquidation of a company, a creditor raises an objection to the claims verified by the liquidation group, it may request the liquidation group to re-verify. If the liquidation group refuses to re-verify, or the creditor still objects to the re-verified claims, and the creditor files a lawsuit with the People's Court against the company for confirmation, the People's Court shall accept the case.

Article 13: Where a creditor fails to declare its claims within the prescribed time limit but makes supplementary declaration before the conclusion of the company's liquidation proceedings, the liquidation group shall register the claims.
The conclusion of the company's liquidation proceedings refers to the confirmation of the liquidation report by the shareholders' meeting, general meeting of shareholders, or the People's Court.

Article 14: The claims declared by the creditor as supplementary may be satisfied according to law from the company's undistributed property. Where the company's undistributed property is insufficient for full satisfaction, and the creditor claims that the shareholders shall use the property they have already obtained in the distribution of residual property for satisfaction, the People's Court shall support the claim, except where the creditor failed to declare its claims within the prescribed time limit due to gross negligence.
Where a creditor or the liquidation group files an application for bankruptcy liquidation with the People's Court on the ground that the company's undistributed property and the property obtained by shareholders in the distribution of residual property are insufficient to satisfy the supplementary declared claims in full, the People's Court shall not accept the application.

Article 15: Where the company conducts voluntary liquidation, the liquidation plan shall be submitted to the shareholders' meeting or the general meeting of shareholders for resolution and confirmation; where the People's Court organizes the liquidation, the liquidation plan shall be submitted to the People's Court for confirmation. The liquidation group shall not execute a liquidation plan that has not been confirmed.
Where the execution of an unconfirmed liquidation plan causes losses to the company or creditors, and the company, shareholders, or creditors claim that the liquidation group members shall bear compensation liability, the People's Court shall support the claim according to law.

Article 16: Where the People's Court organizes the liquidation, the liquidation group shall complete the liquidation within six months from the date of its establishment.
If the liquidation cannot be completed within six months due to special circumstances, the liquidation group shall apply to the People's Court for an extension.

Article 17: Where the liquidation group appointed by the People's Court, when clearing the company's property and preparing the balance sheet and property inventory, discovers that the company's property is insufficient to pay off its debts, it may negotiate with the creditors to formulate a debt repayment plan.
Where the debt repayment plan is confirmed by all creditors and does not harm the interests of other interested parties, the People's Court may, upon application by the liquidation group, issue a ruling to approve it. After the liquidation group pays off the debts in accordance with the repayment plan, it shall apply to the People's Court for a ruling to conclude the liquidation proceedings.
Where the creditors do not confirm the debt repayment plan or the People's Court does not approve it, the liquidation group shall apply to the People's Court for a declaration of bankruptcy according to law.

Article 18: Where the shareholders of a limited liability company, or the directors and controlling shareholders of a joint stock limited company, fail to establish a liquidation group and commence liquidation within the statutory time limit, causing the company's property to depreciate, be lost, damaged, or destroyed, and the creditors claim that they shall bear compensation liability for the company's debts within the scope of the losses caused, the People's Court shall support the claim according to law.
Where the shareholders of a limited liability company, or the directors and controlling shareholders of a joint stock limited company, fail to perform their duties, resulting in the loss of the company's main property, account books, important documents, etc., making liquidation impossible, and the creditors claim that they shall bear joint and several liability for paying off the company's debts, the People's Court shall support the claim according to law.
Where the above circumstances are caused by the actual controller, and the creditors claim that the actual controller shall bear corresponding civil liability for the company's debts, the People's Court shall support the claim according to law.

Article 19: Where, after the dissolution of the company, the shareholders of a limited liability company, the directors and controlling shareholders of a joint stock limited company, and the actual controller of the company maliciously dispose of the company's property, causing losses to creditors, or, without liquidation according to law, obtain the company registration authority to handle the cancellation of legal person registration by means of a false liquidation report, and the creditors claim that they shall bear corresponding compensation liability for the company's debts, the People's Court shall support the claim according to law.

Article 20: The dissolution of a company shall be applied for cancellation registration after the completion of liquidation according to law. Where the company undergoes cancellation registration without liquidation, resulting in the impossibility of liquidation, and the creditors claim that the shareholders of a limited liability company, the directors and controlling shareholders of a joint stock limited company, and the actual controller of the company shall bear liability for paying off the company's debts, the People's Court shall support the claim according to law.
Where the company undergoes cancellation registration without liquidation according to law, and the shareholders or third parties undertake to bear liability for the company's debts when handling the cancellation registration with the company registration authority, and the creditors claim that they shall bear corresponding civil liability for the company's debts, the People's Court shall support the claim according to law.

Article 21: Where there are two or more shareholders of a limited liability company, directors and controlling shareholders of a joint stock limited company, and actual controllers of the company, and one or several of them have borne civil liability in accordance with Article 18 and paragraph 1 of Article 20 of these Provisions, and then claim that the other persons shall share the liability according to the degree of fault, the People's Court shall support the claim according to law.

Article 22: Upon the dissolution of a company, all capital contributions not yet paid by shareholders shall be treated as liquidation property. The capital contributions not yet paid by shareholders include those that have fallen due but are unpaid, as well as those to be paid in installments in accordance with Articles 26 and 80 of the Company Law where the payment term has not yet expired.
Where the company's property is insufficient to pay off its debts, and the creditors claim that the shareholders who have not paid their capital contributions, as well as other shareholders or promoters at the time of the company's establishment, shall bear joint and several liability for paying off the company's debts to the extent of the unpaid capital contributions, the People's Court shall support the claim according to law.

Article 23: Where a member of the liquidation group, when handling liquidation matters, violates laws, administrative regulations, or the company's articles of association, causing losses to the company or creditors, and the company or creditors claim that the member shall bear compensation liability, the People's Court shall support the claim according to law.
Where a shareholder of a limited liability company, or a shareholder of a joint stock limited company individually or collectively holding not less than one percent of the company's shares for a continuous period of not less than 180 days, files a lawsuit with the People's Court against a member of the liquidation group on the ground of the acts described in the preceding paragraph in accordance with paragraph 3 of Article 151 of the Company Law, the People's Court shall accept the case.
Where the company has completed liquidation and been canceled, and the shareholder as described above files a lawsuit directly with the People's Court against the member of the liquidation group as the defendant and other shareholders as third parties by reference to paragraph 3 of Article 151 of the Company Law, the People's Court shall accept the case.

Article 24: Cases concerning lawsuits for dissolution of a company and cases concerning company liquidation shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court of the place where the company is domiciled. The domicile of a company refers to the location of its principal place of business. Where the location of the company's place of business is unclear, the People's Court of the place of its registration shall have jurisdiction.
Primary People's Courts shall have jurisdiction over cases of lawsuits for dissolution and company liquidation of companies registered with the company registration authority of a county, county-level city, or district; Intermediate People's Courts shall have jurisdiction over cases of lawsuits for dissolution and company liquidation of companies registered with the company registration authority of a prefecture, prefecture-level city, or higher.
Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (III)
(Adopted at the 1504th Session of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on December 6, 2010, and amended according to the Decision on Amending the Provisions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China adopted at the 1607th Session of the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court on February 17, 2014)
For the purpose of correctly applying the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, in light of trial practice, the following provisions are formulated concerning the application of law in cases of disputes over company establishment, capital contribution, and confirmation of equity tried by the People's Court.

Article 1: A person who signs the company's articles of association for the purpose of establishing the company, subscribes for capital contributions or shares to the company, and performs the duties of company establishment shall be identified as a promoter of the company, including the shareholders at the time of establishment of a limited liability company.

Article 2: Where a promoter, for the purpose of establishing the company, signs a contract with a third party in its own name, and the counterparty to the contract requests the promoter to bear the contract liability, the People's Court shall support the claim.
Where after the company is established, the company confirms the contract specified in the preceding paragraph, or has actually enjoyed the contractual rights or performed the contractual obligations, and the counterparty requests the company to bear the contract liability, the People's Court shall support the claim.

Article 3: Where a promoter signs a contract with a third party in the name of the company being established, and after the company is established, the counterparty to the contract requests the company to bear the contract liability, the People's Court shall support the claim.
Where after the company is established, there is evidence proving that the promoter signed the contract with the counterparty in the name of the company being established for its own benefit, and the company claims not to bear the contract liability on this ground, the People's Court shall support the claim, except where the counterparty is in good faith.

Article 4: Where a company is not established for any reason, and the creditors request all or part of the promoters to bear joint and several liability for paying the expenses and debts incurred in the act of establishing the company, the People's Court shall support the claim.
Where some promoters have borne liability in accordance with the preceding paragraph and then request the other promoters to share the liability, the People's Court shall order the other promoters to share the liability in proportion to the agreed liability sharing ratio; if there is no agreed liability sharing ratio, in proportion to the agreed capital contribution ratio; if there is no agreed capital contribution ratio, in equal shares.
Where the failure to establish the company is caused by the fault of some promoters, and other promoters claim that the defaulting promoters shall bear the expenses and debts incurred in the act of establishment, the People's Court shall determine the scope of liability of the defaulting party based on the fault situation.

Article 5: Where a promoter causes harm to others in the performance of its duties in establishing the company, and after the company is established, the victim requests the company to bear tort compensation liability, the People's Court shall support the claim; where the company is not established, and the victim requests all promoters to bear joint and several compensation liability, the People's Court shall support the claim.
After the company or a promoter without fault bears compensation liability, it may seek recourse against the promoter at fault.

Article 6: Where a subscriber of a joint stock limited company fails to pay the share capital for the subscribed shares on time, and after being urged by the company's promoters, still fails to pay within a reasonable period, and the company's promoters raise the shares separately, the People's Court shall find the raising valid. Where the subscriber's delay in paying the share capital causes losses to the company, and the company requests the subscriber to bear compensation liability, the People's Court shall support the claim.

Article 7: Where a capital contributor makes a capital contribution with property over which it has no right of disposal, and the parties dispute the validity of the capital contribution act, the People's Court may determine it by reference to Article 106 of the Property Law.
Where a capital contribution is made in monetary form from illegally obtained proceeds such as embezzlement, bribery, misappropriation, or defalcation, and equity is obtained, when investigating and punishing the illegal act, the equity shall be disposed of by auction or sale.

Article 8: Where a capital contributor makes a capital contribution with a land use right obtained by allocation, or with a land use right that is encumbered with a right, and the company, other shareholders, or company creditors claim that the capital contributor has not performed its capital contribution obligation, the People's Court shall order the party to handle the land change procedures or remove the encumbrance within a specified reasonable period; if the party fails to do so within the time limit, the People's Court shall find that the capital contributor has not fully performed its capital contribution obligation according to law.

Article 9: Where a capital contributor makes a capital contribution with non-monetary property without having it appraised according to law, and the company, other shareholders, or company creditors request a finding that the capital contributor has not performed its capital contribution obligation, the People's Court shall entrust a legally qualified appraisal institution to appraise the property. If the appraised value is significantly lower than the value set in the company's articles of association, the People's Court shall find that the capital contributor has not fully performed its capital contribution obligation according to law.

Article 10: Where a capital contributor makes a capital contribution with property such as a house, land use right, or intellectual property that requires registration of title, and has delivered the property to the company for use but has not completed the formalities for change of title, and the company, other shareholders, or company creditors claim that the capital contributor has not performed its capital contribution obligation, the People's Court shall order the party to complete the formalities for change of title within a specified reasonable period; if the formalities are completed within the aforementioned period, the People's Court shall find that the capital contributor has performed its capital contribution obligation; where the capital contributor claims that it enjoys corresponding shareholder rights from the time it actually delivered the property to the company for use, the People's Court shall support the claim.
Where a capital contributor makes a capital contribution with the property described in the preceding paragraph, and has completed the formalities for change of title but has not delivered the property to the company for use, and the company or other shareholders claim that it shall deliver the property to the company and shall not enjoy corresponding shareholder rights before actual delivery, the People's Court shall support the claim.

Article 13 Where a shareholder has not performed or has not fully performed its capital contribution obligation, and the company or other shareholders request it to fully perform its capital contribution obligation to the company according to law, the People's Court shall support such request.
Where creditors of the company request a shareholder that has not performed or has not fully performed its capital contribution obligation to bear supplementary compensation liability within the scope of the unpaid capital and its interest for the part of the company's debts that cannot be satisfied, the People's Court shall support such request; if the shareholder that has not performed or has not fully performed its capital contribution obligation has already borne the aforesaid liability, and other creditors make the same request, the People's Court shall not support such request.
Where a shareholder has not performed or has not fully performed its capital contribution obligation at the time of the company's incorporation, and a plaintiff bringing an action in accordance with paragraph 1 or paragraph 2 of this Article requests the company's promoters to bear joint and several liability with the defendant shareholder, the People's Court shall support such request; after the promoters have borne liability, they may seek recourse from the defendant shareholder.
Where a shareholder has not performed or has not fully performed its capital contribution obligation at the time of a capital increase, and a plaintiff bringing an action in accordance with paragraph 1 or paragraph 2 of this Article requests the directors or senior officers who failed to fulfill the obligation under Article 147(1) of the Company Law and thereby caused the capital contribution not to be fully paid up to bear corresponding liability, the People's Court shall support such request; after such directors or senior officers have borne liability, they may seek recourse from the defendant shareholder.

Article 14 Where a shareholder withdraws its capital contribution, and the company or other shareholders request it to return the capital contribution and its interest to the company, and request other shareholders, directors, senior officers, or actual controllers who assisted in the withdrawal of capital contribution to bear joint and several liability therefor, the People's Court shall support such request.
Where creditors of the company request the shareholder that withdrew its capital contribution to bear supplementary compensation liability within the scope of the withdrawn capital and its interest for the part of the company's debts that cannot be satisfied, and request other shareholders, directors, senior officers, or actual controllers who assisted in the withdrawal of capital contribution to bear joint and several liability therefor, the People's Court shall support such request; if the shareholder that withdrew its capital contribution has already borne the aforesaid liability, and other creditors make the same request, the People's Court shall not support such request.

Article 15 After a contributor has made a capital contribution with non-monetary property that satisfies the statutory conditions, if the contributed property depreciates due to market changes or other objective factors, and the company, other shareholders, or creditors of the company request the contributor to bear the liability to make up the capital contribution, the People's Court shall not support such request, unless the parties have agreed otherwise.

Article 16 Where a shareholder has not performed or has not fully performed its capital contribution obligation or has withdrawn its capital contribution, and the company, in accordance with the company's articles of association or a resolution of the shareholders' meeting, imposes corresponding reasonable restrictions on such shareholder's rights, including the right to claim profit distribution, the preemptive right to subscribe for new shares, and the right to claim distribution of residual property, if the shareholder requests a determination that such restrictions are invalid, the People's Court shall not support such request.

Article 17 Where a shareholder of a limited liability company has not performed its capital contribution obligation or has withdrawn all of its capital contribution, and after the company has demanded by notice that the shareholder make the contribution or return the contribution, the shareholder still fails to make or return the contribution within a reasonable period, and the company terminates the shareholder's shareholder status by a resolution of the shareholders' meeting, if the shareholder requests confirmation that such termination is invalid, the People's Court shall not support such request.
In the circumstances described in the preceding paragraph, the People's Court shall clarify in its judgment that the company shall promptly carry out statutory capital reduction procedures or have other shareholders or third parties make the corresponding capital contribution. Before the statutory capital reduction procedures are carried out or other shareholders or third parties make the corresponding capital contribution, if creditors of the company, in accordance with Article 13 or Article 14 of these Provisions, request the relevant parties to bear corresponding liability, the People's Court shall support such request.

Article 18 Where a shareholder of a limited liability company transfers its equity interests without having performed or fully performed its capital contribution obligation, and the transferee knew or should have known of such circumstance, if the company requests the shareholder to perform its capital contribution obligation and the transferee to bear joint and several liability therefor, the People's Court shall support such request; if creditors of the company bring an action against the shareholder in accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 13 of these Provisions and also request the aforesaid transferee to bear joint and several liability therefor, the People's Court shall support such request.
Where the transferee has borne liability in accordance with the preceding paragraph and seeks recourse from the shareholder that has not performed or has not fully performed its capital contribution obligation, the People's Court shall support such request, unless the parties have agreed otherwise.

Article 19 Where a company's shareholder has not performed or has not fully performed its capital contribution obligation or has withdrawn its capital contribution, and the company or other shareholders request it to fully perform its capital contribution obligation or return the contribution, if the defendant shareholder defends on the ground of limitation of action, the People's Court shall not support such defense.
Where the creditor's claim of the company's creditor has not exceeded the limitation period, and the creditor requests a shareholder that has not performed or has not fully performed its capital contribution obligation or has withdrawn its capital contribution to bear compensation liability in accordance with paragraph 2 of Article 13 or paragraph 2 of Article 14 of these Provisions, if the defendant shareholder defends on the ground that the obligation to make capital contribution or return contribution has exceeded the limitation period, the People's Court shall not support such defense.

Article 20 Where a dispute arises between parties as to whether a capital contribution obligation has been performed, and the plaintiff provides evidence that raises reasonable doubt as to whether the shareholder has performed its capital contribution obligation, the defendant shareholder shall bear the burden of adducing evidence that it has performed its capital contribution obligation.

Article 21 Where a party brings a lawsuit before the People's Court requesting confirmation of its shareholder status, the company shall be named as the defendant, and persons having an interest in the equity interests in dispute in the case shall participate in the action as third parties.

Article 23 After a party has performed its capital contribution obligation according to law or has acquired equity interests by succession according to law, if the company fails to issue a capital contribution certificate, record the party in the register of shareholders, and register with the company registration authority in accordance with Articles 31 and 32 of the Company Law, and the party requests the company to perform the aforesaid obligations, the People's Court shall support such request.

Article 24 Where an actual contributor and a nominal contributor in a limited liability company enter into a contract stipulating that the actual contributor shall make the capital contribution and enjoy the investment rights and interests, with the nominal contributor being the nominal shareholder, and a dispute arises between the actual contributor and the nominal shareholder over the validity of the contract, if there are no circumstances set forth in Article 52 of the Contract Law, the People's Court shall hold that the contract is valid.
Where a dispute arises between the actual contributor and the nominal shareholder as described in the preceding paragraph over the ownership of investment rights and interests, and the actual contributor asserts its rights against the nominal shareholder on the ground that it has actually performed its capital contribution obligation, the People's Court shall support such claim. Where the nominal shareholder denies the rights of the actual contributor on the ground of the records in the register of shareholders or the registration with the company registration authority, the People's Court shall not support such defense.
Where the actual contributor, without the consent of more than half of the company's other shareholders, requests the company to change the shareholder, issue a capital contribution certificate, record it in the register of shareholders, record it in the articles of association, and register with the company registration authority, the People's Court shall not support such request.

Article 25 Where a nominal shareholder transfers, pledges, or otherwise disposes of the equity interests registered in its name, and the actual contributor requests a determination that the disposition of the equity interests is invalid on the ground that it has the actual right to the equity interests, the People's Court may handle the matter by reference to Article 106 of the Property Law.
Where the disposition of equity interests by the nominal shareholder causes losses to the actual contributor, and the actual contributor requests the nominal shareholder to bear compensation liability, the People's Court shall support such request.

Article 26 Where a creditor of the company requests a shareholder registered with the company registration authority to bear supplementary compensation liability within the scope of the unpaid capital and its interest for the part of the company's debts that cannot be satisfied, on the ground that the shareholder has not performed its capital contribution obligation, and the shareholder defends on the ground that it is merely a nominal shareholder and not the actual contributor, the People's Court shall not support such defense.
Where the nominal shareholder has borne compensation liability in accordance with the preceding paragraph and seeks recourse from the actual contributor, the People's Court shall support such request.

Article 27 Where, after the transfer of equity interests but before the change registration has been completed with the company registration authority, the original shareholder transfers, pledges, or otherwise disposes of the equity interests still registered in its name, and the transferee shareholder requests a determination that the disposition of the equity interests is invalid on the ground that it has the actual right to the equity interests, the People's Court may handle the matter by reference to Article 106 of the Property Law.
Where the disposition of equity interests by the original shareholder causes losses to the transferee shareholder, and the transferee shareholder requests the original shareholder to bear compensation liability and requests the directors, senior officers, or actual controllers who are at fault for the failure to timely complete the change registration to bear corresponding liability, the People's Court shall support such request; if the transferee shareholder is also at fault for the failure to timely complete the change registration, the liability of the aforesaid directors, senior officers, or actual controllers may be appropriately reduced.

Article 28 Where a person uses another person's name to make a capital contribution and registers such other person as a shareholder with the company registration authority, the person who made the false registration shall bear corresponding liability; if the company, other shareholders, or creditors of the company request the person falsely registered as a shareholder to bear the liability to make up the capital contribution or to bear compensation liability for the part of the company's debts that cannot be satisfied, on the ground that the capital contribution obligation has not been performed, the People's Court shall not support such request.
